title: Learning Intrinsic Dynamics in Latent World Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.21612v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Learning intrinsic dynamics---the relationship between actions and their consequences---is essential for world models. However, visual variations unrelated to the underlying control process can obscure this relationship in learned representations. We investigate the connection between action predictability, defined as the ability to reconstruct an action from consecutive latent states, and the preservation of intrinsic dynamics. Our central hypothesis is that encouraging action predictability discourages representations from discarding the distinctions between different actions and their consequences. We provide two complementary forms of evidence for this connection. Theoretically, we derive a positive lower bound on squared inverse prediction error when the encoder merges distinguishable outcomes of different actions from the same state and appearance, and show that forward prediction can still be exact on those transitions. translated_title: 在潜在世界模型中学习内在动力学
translated_abstract: 学习内在动力学——即动作与其结果之间的关系——对世界模型而言至关重要。然而，与底层控制过程无关的视觉变化可能会在学到的表征中掩盖这种关系。我们研究了动作可预测性（定义为从连续的潜在状态中重建动作的能力）与内在动力学保持之间的联系。我们的核心假设是：鼓励动作可预测性可以阻止表征丢弃不同动作及其结果之间的区别。我们为这一联系提供了两种互补形式的证据。在理论上，当编码器将来自相同状态和外观的不同动作的可区分结果合并时，我们推导出了平方逆预测误差的正下界，并证明前向预测在这些转移上仍然可以保持精确。在实证上……
tldr: 本文提出并验证了动作可预测性（从连续潜在状态重建动作的能力）与内在动力学保持之间的联系，证明鼓励动作可预测性可防止世界模型表征丢弃不同动作及其结果之间的本质区别，并从理论下界和实证两方面提供了证据。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes that encouraging action predictability—the ability to reconstruct actions from consecutive latent states—preserves intrinsic dynamics in latent world models, preventing representations from discarding distinctions between different actions and their consequences, with both theoretical lower-bound and empirical evidence.
